title: Adaptive precision selector + prefill safeguard to mitigate FlashAttn v3 latency spike
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We observed a reproducible latency regression for long-context workloads after integrating FlashAttention v3 kernels into the runtime. The regression manifests as a 30-120ms decode tail latency spike at sequence lengths >= 1536 for several GPT-family and LLaMA-like models in mixed-precision (FP16/AMP) configurations.

Impact:
- Affects hosted API customers using long-context prompts, increasing 95th/99th latency and causing transient SLO violations for conversational workloads.
- Observed both in Hosted (canary region us-west-2b) and Dedicated pools with Ampere A100 80GB.

Investigation highlights:
- Repro steps attached below reproduce a consistent spike during the prefill->decode transition when a kernel switch to a v3 tiling variant occurs.
- Memory profiler shows increased temporary allocation churn and fragmentation when v3's default tiling is chosen for certain sequence lengths.
- Autotuner (kernel selector) currently scores kernels based on average tokens/s without accounting for transient allocation costs during prefill boundary transitions.
- Hypothesis: v3 chooses a higher-throughput tile for long sequences, but the memory pattern induces allocator chasing and cross-SM synchronization causing decode tail latency spikes on warmup.

Proposed mitigation (short-term):
1) Implement a "prefill safeguard" policy in the runtime that forces a conservative kernel choice for the first N decode requests after a prefill boundary (configurable; default N=3). This avoids switching to aggressive v3 variants until steady-state streaming is confirmed.
2) Add a fast path in the selector to prefer lower-fragmentation kernels when sequence-length delta across requests exceeds a threshold.
3) Emit telemetry around kernel switch events, prefill boundaries, allocation counts, and per-request tail-latency to validate effectiveness.

Proposed long-term fixes:
- Extend the autotuner scoring model to include allocation churn and tail-latency penalties (sequence-aware cost model).
- Work with upstream FlashAttention maintainers to explore tiling/allocator-friendly variants and reduce transient memory pressure.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary deployments show 95/99 latency for affected models reduced to within 5% of v2 baseline for long-context workloads on runtime-1.24.
- Selector logs and telemetry demonstrate reduced kernel switch churn at prefill boundaries.
- Unit + integration tests added to catch regressions.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Checkout runtime canary branch: git checkout canary/flashattn-v3-smoke
2) Start local perf harness with long context profile: ./dev/perf_harness --model gpt-like-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --prefill 1024 --decode-steps 512 --fp16
3) Observe tail-latency using the provided tracer: ./tools/trace_collect --pid <runtime_pid> --output trace.json
4) Compare kernel selection events in logs and look for a kernel switch at prefill->decode boundary and a latency spike within the next 3 decode requests.

Attachments / links:
- Internal perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/prefill-v3-spike
- Perf trace sample: drive.redwood.ai/attachments/ENG-95123/trace-sample-2026-02-16.json
- Draft runtime PR (safeguard): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4992
- Related investigation tickets: ENG-84211 (quantized-v3 routing audit), ENG-4721 (flash kernel integration notes)

Notes:
- This ticket is scoped for a short-term mitigation + telemetry + test coverage. Follow-up ENG-95124 will implement autotuner score changes and upstream collaboration.
